AI-first debt resolution platform Credfix has raised Rs 16.1 crore in a seed funding round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with participation from Stargazer. Before this round, Credfix had raised Rs 4.5 crore from K2 Capital, Invstt Trust and a group of angel investors. The fresh capital will be used to accelerate product development, strengthen its AI capabilities and expand its borrower support network across India, Credfix said in a press release. Founded in 2025 by Ranjan Agarwal, Neeraj Kulkarni and Ayush Kedia, Credfix is an AI-powered financial recovery platform that helps borrowers understand their debt, assess repayment options and navigate interactions with lenders. Its offerings include debt assessment, loan resolution, loan consolidation and AI-powered legal assistance. The platform has three key AI-led solutions: Risi, an AI financial assistant; Neytra, an AI call shield; and an AI legal assistant. Risi helps borrowers understand their debt and explore resolution options, while Neytra assists with recovery-related calls. The legal assistant helps borrowers understand legal notices, prepare draft responses for their review and identify possible next steps. Credfix said it aims to support borrowers across the debt resolution lifecycle, from early signs of financial distress to structured resolution and financial rehabilitation. The platform helps users assess their financial obligations, evaluate available options, communicate with lenders and understand legal notices. The startup claims to currently serve more than 2 lakh borrowers representing over Rs 4,000 crore in aggregate outstanding debt. Around 40% of its users are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. The debt resolution and collections segment has seen growing technology adoption in India. Sunfox Technologies, the Dehradun-based medtech company behind the Spandan portable ECG platform, has raised $7 million (approx. Rs 67 crore) in a Series A funding round co-led by Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital. The startup had previously raised Rs 15 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Venture Catalysts, with participation from Finvolve through the IA Growth Opportunities Fund I and Brew Opportunities Fund, Universal Group, RP Singhvi Group and others in August 2024. It also secured investments from all five Sharks in the first season of Shark Tank India. The fresh funds will be used for the next phase of growth, including expanding its presence across India, developing global go-to-market capabilities, scaling the organisation and continuing investments in research and development, Sunfox said in a press release. Founded in 2016 by Rajat Jain, Arpit Jain, Saurabh Badola, Nitin Chandola and Sabit Rawat, Sunfox Technologies develops portable and AI-enabled healthcare solutions, with a focus on diagnostic access, particularly in cardiac care. Its flagship Spandan series is a portable, medical-grade ECG platform designed for use across hospitals, clinics, telemedicine networks and home-based patient monitoring. The platform enables ECGs to be recorded closer to patients and can flag cardiac patterns that may require further medical attention. Over the past decade, Sunfox has developed a range of Spandan ECG solutions for personal, clinical and institutional use, with applications across home-based ECG recording, clinics, hospitals, public-health programmes and remote-care networks. Sunfox said it has expanded its presence to more than 15 countries, while its products have reached healthcare providers across more than 1,800 PIN codes in India. Hopit â a continual-learning lab Hopit New Hopper places #2 in JevBench's Jev-class ranking â A continual-learning lab AI that gets better at its job by doing it. We build models and harnesses that learn new tasks, keep what they already know, and improve inside the enterprises that use them. Work with us â Join us The problem Today, an AI system is trained once and then frozen. A company should be able to teach its AI a new task, correct its mistakes, and watch it build an understanding of the business that compounds. That almost never happens. Models are fine-tuned once and left alone. The software around them is written by hand and rarely changes. Every correction an expert makes is gone the moment the session ends. Capability is also getting cheap. When everyone can rent the same frontier model, the advantage moves to what only you can learn â and those lessons live in your own work, not on the open web. Our approach Two halves of one system, learning together. 01 Â· The model Learns new capabilities Not a one-off fine-tune, but a repeatable process of learning, evaluation and controlled updates â new tasks learned while earlier skills, and the ability to keep learning, are retained. 02 Â· The harness Learns how to do the work The tools, memory, checks and workflows around the model learn from successful outcomes and expert corrections, propose better ways of working, and test those changes before they are used. A better harness produces more useful experience to learn from. A better model takes on harder work and improves its own workflows. That recursive loop is what we are building. What we have shown Early, measured, and published with its caveats. #2 JevBench Â· Jev-class Hopper, our 4B decision model, ranks second in JevBench's Jev-class capability ranking â 63.5 against the leader's 64.7 â with the highest calibration of any system in the top six.
